title: When the Guard Adds Nothing: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for LLM‑Produced Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=300 paired tasks) that measured whether a deterministic generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R) pipeline increases the probability that an LLM‑produced vendor CLI configuration passes a conservative deterministic validator, relative to direct LLM generation. The preregistration froze a single shared initial candidate per task (one generator call shared by both arms) and allowed a bounded guarded policy that performs at most one automatic repair call for the guarded arm when the shared initial fails. Under the declared generator snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini) and the supplied 300‑task multi‑vendor manifest, every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator: baseline = 300/300; guarded = 300/300. The paired contingency table is n11 = 300, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because no initial failures occurred, the preregistered single‑repair policy was never invoked. We release the full preregistration, manifest, model configuration, raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts with canonical SHA‑256 hashes to enable exact reproduction and controlled follow‑ups.

sections.introduction: Generative language models that translate operator intent into vendor CLI changes promise to accelerate NetOps, but operational deployment requires high confidence that generated configurations preserve safety invariants. A widely proposed operational architecture adds a deterministic validator and bounded automatic repair: generate → validate → (if fail) repair. Intuitively, repair can reduce unsafe outputs, but its marginal benefit depends on the generator error rate in the target intent distribution and the repair budget. We designed and preregistered a narrow, machine‑readable confirmatory experiment that isolates the incremental effect of a bounded single automatic repair call when the same initial candidate is shared between baseline and guarded arms. The shared‑initial paired design removes generator sampling variance as a confounder and therefore measures only the value added by the bounded repair step given the exact same initial candidate. We deployed the preregistered plan end‑to‑end and archived all artifacts (task manifest, model configuration, provider traces, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis outputs) with canonical SHA‑256 hashes for exact reproduction.
sections.related_work: Prior work has explored LLM‑assisted intent‑to‑configuration, validator‑anchored guardrails, and tool‑assisted self‑refinement. Representative verified sources that motivated our conservative validator design and preregistration strategy include Nguyen et al., "Intent‑Based Network Configuration Using Large Language Models" (Nem, 2024; DOI: 10.1002/nem.2313), CNSM/NetOps automation prototypes (Chakraborty et al., CNSM 2024), tool‑augmented self‑refinement pipelines (INTERACSPARQL), and deterministic BGP/config verification systems (Weitz et al., 2016). We explicitly used primary sources where available and archived a reference verification record for every cited item (see Cited Record Ids). Our contribution differs: it preregisters a paired shared‑initial design and executes it with a conservative deterministic validator, publishing all execution artifacts to enable exact replay and targeted follow‑ups.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a machine‑readable experimental plan (study_hosted_netops_gvr_v1_cnd_7a3f2b1e; SHA‑256 = a85d66d4c6ce2275e2d8c820f96c610532dbb5452bebb3fe108848f9dc38cdf6). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (per‑task probability difference that the guarded arm yields a validator pass vs the baseline arm, paired across tasks). Design: paired paired tasks n=300; for each task a single shared initial candidate was generated by the declared generator (gpt‑5‑mini). Baseline outcome = validator(initial). Guarded outcome = validator(initial) or, if initial fails, a single automatic repair generation is attempted and the repaired candidate revalidated. Per‑task budgets: baseline ≤1 call; guarded ≤2 calls. All seeds, prompts, and repair templates were frozen and archived prior to execution (preregistration manifest and model_configuration.json are archived).
sections.results: Execution and bookkeeping. The run executed exactly per the preregistration. Planned episodes = 600 (300 tasks × 2 arms with shared initial); completed episodes = 600; failed episodes = 0. Model calls used = 300 (one shared initial generation per task; no repair calls were consumed). All raw outputs, provider traces, scoring artifacts, and SHA‑256 hashes are archived in the execution bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json; representative artifact: execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a722e6a91dd2abd7baca45a2aefb41e124b049124d5ea2632cb4b3; model configuration: execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa).
sections.discussion: Primary confirmatory outcome. Every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator: baseline_success_count = 300/300; guarded_success_count = 300/300. The paired contingency table is n11=300, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = a39fd3386c945cae095f2f310ead1f21ac600f8b2492bcd49b664c8da5782aa0). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. Because no initial failures occurred, the preregistered single‑repair policy was never invoked and repair_call_count = 0. Statistical interpretation. The paired design cleanly measures the incremental effect of a bounded repair on the exact same generator output. Under the observed ceiling (zero discordant pairs), the guarded policy cannot increase the deterministic pass rate; the observed null effect (estimate = 0.00) and degenerate CI reflect the data and not an analysis error.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment to quantify the marginal value of a bounded single automatic repair step in a generate–validate–repair pipeline for LLM‑produced vendor CLI fragments. For the supplied 300‑task manifest, prompt, and gpt‑5‑mini snapshot every shared initial candidate passed a conservative deterministic validator, so the single‑repair step was not invoked and produced no measurable benefit (paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar p = 1.00; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00]). This outcome demonstrates that the marginal utility of G‑V‑R depends on generator error frequency in the deployment task bank. We publish the full preregistration, task manifest, provider traces, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts with canonical SHA‑256 hashes to enable exact reproduction and controlled follow‑ups that vary task hardness, generator prompt, model snapshot, or repair budget.

limitations: Single model snapshot (gpt-5-mini) evaluated — results do not generalize to other models or model versions.

Deterministic validator implements a conservative subset of operational hazards (syntactic checks, interface and workflow invariants) and omits dynamic/emulation‑level checks and deeper routing semantics.

Curated 300‑task manifest may not include adversarial or out‑of‑distribution failure modes; under the chosen prompt and model snapshot every shared initial candidate passed the validator (ceiling effect), limiting the ability to measure G‑V‑R improvements under the preregistered one‑repair policy.

Shared initial‑candidate design (preregistered) fixes the same initial generation for both arms to isolate repair effect; this reduces sensitivity to generator variability and can mask repair value when the generator is already accurate on the task set.
Only a single automatic repair attempt was permitted per task; iterative or human‑in‑the‑loop repair policies were not evaluated.
Automated contamination detection cannot eliminate memorization risk entirely; the preregistered contamination summary reported zero flagged pairs but residual uncertainty remains.
